description: DE: Die bestehende Instandhaltungsanlage am Standort Giesshübel in Zürich ist technisch und betrieblich überholt und erfüllt die zukünftigen Anforderungen an modernes Rollmaterial nicht mehr. Vorgesehen ist der Rückbau der bestehenden Anlage und der Neubau einer zukunftsfähigen Instandhaltungsanlage mit zwei rund 130 m langen Gleisen und Waschanlage. Das Projekt befindet sich in einem innerstädtischen, räumlich stark begrenzten Umfeld mit komplexen Rahmenbedingungen. Gesucht wird eine erfahrene Projektsteuerung / Bauherrenvertretung zur ganzheitlichen Führung des Projekts und optimalen Begleitung dieses vielseitigen komplexen Projektes. Ziel der Beschaffung ist die Beauftragung einer erfahrenen Projektsteuerung / Bauherrenvertretung, welche den Bauherrn bei der Planung und Realisierung der neuen Instandhaltungsanlage ganzheitlich unterstützt und eine zielgerichtete Steuerung von Kosten, Terminen, Qualität und Risiken sicherstellt. Weitere Details zum genauen Umfang entnehmen Sie dem Dokument B1_Lastenheft. FR: L’installation de maintenance existante sur le site de Giesshübel à Zurich est devenue obsolète tant sur le plan technique qu’opérationnel et ne répond plus aux exigences futures du matériel roulant moderne. Le projet prévoit le démantèlement de l’installation existante et la construction d’une nouvelle installation de maintenance pérenne et adaptée aux besoins futurs, comprenant deux voies ferrées d’environ 130 mètres de long ainsi qu’une installation de lavage. Le projet s’inscrit dans un environnement urbain dense, caractérisé par un espace fortement limité et des conditions-cadres complexes. Nous recherchons une équipe expérimentée en gestion de projet / représentation du maître d’ouvrage, capable d’assurer la conduite globale du projet et d’accompagner de manière optimale sa réalisation, compte tenu de sa diversité et de sa complexité. L’objectif du présent marché est de mandater un prestataire expérimenté en gestion de projet / représentation du maître d’ouvrage, chargé d’assister le maître d’ouvrage de manière globale lors de la planification et de la réalisation de la nouvelle installation de maintenance, tout en garantissant un pilotage efficace des coûts, des délais, de la qualité et des risques. Pour plus de détails concernant l’étendue exacte des prestations, veuillez vous référer au document B1_Lastenheft. ENG: The existing maintenance facility at the Giesshübel site in Zurich has become technically and operationally obsolete and no longer meets the future requirements of modern rolling stock. The project the dismantling of the existing facility and the construction of a new, future-proof maintenance facility comprising two railway tracks, each approximately 130 metres long, as well as a washing facility. The project is situated in a densely built-up urban environment with severely limited space and complex boundary conditions. We are seeking an experienced project management / client representation team to provide overall project leadership and ensure optimal support throughout this multifaceted and complex project. The objective of this procurement is to appoint an experienced project management / client representation provider to offer comprehensive support to the client throughout the planning and implementation of the new maintenance facility, ensuring effective management and control of costs, schedules, quality and risks. Further details regarding the exact scope of services can be found in document B1_Lastenheft.

Der verbleibende Torso ist nicht mehr sanierungsfähig, sodass an anderer Stelle ein Ersatzneubau mit 12 Stellplätzen realisiert werden soll. Die neue Lage südlich der Ahr befindet sich in Sichtweite des heutigen Feuerwehrgebäudes. Durch die Umlegung des Feuerwehrgebäudes soll in Zukunft die Erreichbarkeit aller Gebiete auch bei extremen Hochwasser durch die Feuerwehr sichergestellt werden. Im Rahmen von Los 070 wird die Gebäudeautomation ausgeschrieben. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme aller Mess-, Steuer- und Regeltechnikkomponenten einschließlich Feldgeräten, Automationsstationen, Netzwerktechnik und Schaltschränken. Zudem sind die vollständige Verkabelung, die Einrichtung der Gebäudeleittechnik, die Programmierung, Prüfungen, Dokumentation sowie die Einweisung des Bedienpersonals auszuführen. Alle Arbeiten erfolgen gemäß VOB/C und den geltenden Normen und Richtlinien, um einen sicheren und zuverlässigen Betrieb der neuen Feuerwache sicherzustellen.

description: Ce concours a pour objectif la désignation du/des lauréat(s) en vue de la passation du marché de maître d'oeuvre pour l'opération de restructuration du service restauration au Lycée du Parc (69 - Lyon). title: Zukunft Oper – Hauptspielstätte
description:
Opernhaus Zürich AG, together with the Building Department (Hochbauamt) and the Cultural Affairs Office of the Canton of Zurich, is planning the refurbishment and expansion of the Zurich Opera House. The selective competition “Zukunft Oper – Hauptspielstätte” (Future Opera – Main Venue) encompasses the existing opera house and the extension building at Sechseläutenplatz. The aim is to modernise the cultural institution’s infrastructure to meet the needs of future generations while making the venue more accessible and attractive to the public.


The procedure will be conducted as a selective, single-stage project competition based on the SIA Regulations 142/2025. A maximum of 25 teams will be selected through a prequalification process covering the disciplines of architecture, construction management, structural engineering and landscape architecture. The selected teams are free to strengthen their teams during the competition phase by engaging specialists of their choice in theatre and operational planning, food and beverage facilities planning, sustainability, energy and building services engineering (heating, ventilation, air conditioning, sanitary and electrical systems), fire safety and building physics.

title: France – Public road transport services – DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC RELATIVE A LA GESTION ET L’EXPLOITATIONDES SERVICES DE MOBILITE ET DE TRANSPORT DE VOYAGEURS SUR LETERRITOIRE DE CHATEAUROUX METROPOLE
description: La consultation a pour objet de déléguer la gestion et l’exploitation des services de mobilité et de transport de voyageurs sur le ressort territorial de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole (Réseau Horizon) Châteauroux Métropole, autorité Organisatrice de la mobilité est autorité délégante. Les missions déléguées sont les suivantes: Offre de base : Exploitation et gestion des services de mobilité et de transports publics de personnes et à l’échelle du territoire communautaire selon les principes définis à l’article 5.1 du document programme. Les candidats devront obligatoirement répondre à l’offre de base et à l'option obligatoire.• Option obligatoire :Option N°1 : Exploitation et gestion d’un service de location de vélos L’option est décrite à l’article 5.2 du document programme. L’Autorité Délégante précisera, avant la remise de l'offre finale si l'option est levée. Le Délégataire assurera la gestion de ces services pour une durée de six (6) ans, à compter du 01/01/2028 et jusqu’au 31/12/2033 dans le cadre d’une délégation de service public (DSP) au sein du périmètre contractuel. Lieu d’exécution : Territoire de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole(département de l’Indre). L’estimation de la valeur du contrat de concession est de 45 millions d’euros HT valeur décembre 2026 sur la durée du contrat. Les missions attendues sont l'organisation, la production et la commercialisation des services, ainsi que la réalisation de l'offre de transport et la maintenance des véhicules et outils de production.Le délégataire assurera en outre la gestion de la relation avec les usagers des transports scolaires qui sont assurés par le biais de marchés publics en cours. La future DSP intègre la gestion et l'exploitation des services de transport suivants sur l’ensemble du périmètre de l’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole : • Le réseau de transport en commun « Horizon » composé aujourd’hui de 12 lignes régulières, • Le service de transport adapté à la demande, « Handibus », à destination des personnes à mobilité réduite sur le périmètre de CM .Pour cette gestion déléguée, la collectivité met à la disposition du délégataire : • Un dépôt de bus réceptionné en 2021 avec une capacité de stationnement de 80 véhicules, équipé de bureaux, d’un atelier de maintenance, de stations de lavage et de carburant et d’équipements de recharge de véhicule électrique; • 31 autobus standard, 5 autobus articulé, 2 midibus. Ces véhicules sont équipés d’équipements de suivi par système SAEIV et cellules de comptage voyageurs. Plusieurs véhicules standard et articulés électriques ont également été commandés. • 2 midibus accessibles et équipés pour accueillir des PMR • Un Site Internet https://www.bushorizon.com/ La présente concession est passée sur le fondement du règlement 1370/2007 et de la directive 2014/23/CEE. La directive 2014/25/UE citée dans le présent avis concerne les marchés des secteurs spéciaux est non les concessions , elle ne s'applique pas à la présente consultation.

title: Client Representation & Project Management for the New SZU Headquarters and the New Maintenance Facility
description:
ENG: The existing maintenance facility at the Giesshübel site in Zurich has become technically and operationally obsolete and no longer meets the future requirements of modern rolling stock.

The project предусматриes the dismantling of the existing facility and the construction of a new, future-proof maintenance facility comprising two railway tracks, each approximately 130 metres long, as well as a washing facility. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing administrative and/or educational purposes, or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., technical skills / job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). Parking is limited on the campus and if redevelopment would result in significantly increased demand for parking, parking must be included within the footprint. For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose an asset at the East Orange VAMC Campus under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. East Orange VA Medical Center Background The East Orange VA Medical Center located at 385 Tremont Avenue, East Orange, NJ 07018-1023 includes ~34 acres situated on a knoll at South Center Street and Tremont Avenue, 228 feet above sea level. The campus overlooks a residential area with views of the Manhattan skyline on the horizon. The grounds are in four municipalities: Orange, East Orange, South Orange, and Newark. The site formerly belonged to the Bamberger estate, which was endowed originally to Princeton University and in turn, sold to a private owner and then purchased by the government. Recognizing the need for a medical facility to serve Veterans in metropolitan areas, Congress approved and funded the facility in 1943. The VAMC opened in July 1952. The hospital provides primary care and specialty health services, including homeless Veteran care, mental health care, skin care (dermatology), dental care, digestive care (gastroenterology), cardiology, eye health and vision care (ophthalmology and optometry), palliative and hospice care, returning service member care, Veteran readiness and employment programs, and more. description: The Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) issues solicitation N00024-27-R-5002 for the execution of the USS DONALD COOK (DDG 75) FY27 Docking Selected Restricted Availability (DSRA). This availability include all labor, supervision, facilities, equipment, production, testing and quality assurance necessary to prepare for and accomplish the CNO Availability. The CNO Availability will require highly capable contractors with substantial facilities, including dry dock, pier and human resources capable of completing, coordinating and integrating multiple areas of ship maintenance, repair and modernization of an Arleigh Burke-class (DDG) Aegis guided missile destroyer class ship for the United States Navy. This availability is being competed on a coast wide basis (East and Gulf coasts), without limiting the place of performance to the ships homeport. This is expected to be awarded as one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price contract. title: Residential Reentry Center (RRC) and Home Confinement Services located within Sacramento County and other border counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility.
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes Residential Reentry Center Services located within Sacramento County and other border Counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 16 beds in which 14 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females and an estimated maximum 40 bed facility in which 34 beds will be designated for males and 6 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 placements and an estimated maximum 20 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. The closing date of 15BRRC26R00000019 is January 08, 2027 at 2:00pm EST. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

title: F-15EX Missile Warning System
description: The Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Fighters & Advanced Aircraft Directorate (AFLCMC/WA), F?15 System Program Office (AFLCMC/WAQ), Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB) is seeking sources for the procurement of an operationally qualified threat missile launch and approach warning system for rapid integration into the United States Air Force (USAF) F-15EX Eagle II fighter aircraft. INTRODUCTION: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT to acquire a missile warning system (MWS) to be integrated into the F-15EX fleet. The system must alert the F-15EX aircrew to missile threats without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six pre-existing sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. The MWS must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel. In accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research, AFLCMC/WAQ is seeking information for potential sources for an integrated MWS solution for the F-15EX. This publication is intended to elicit responses from sources with knowledge, skills, data, equipment, access to appropriate facilities, and the capacity to meet the Air Force�s requirements. The dollar value and period of performance (PoP) for the contract will be commensurate with the requirement. This contract effort is subject to RFO 52.232-18, Availability of Funds. 1.1 SOURCES SOUGHT INFORMATION 1.2 DISCLAIMER: THIS?SOURCES SOUGHT?IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY.? THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB).?IN ACCORDANCE WITH?RFO 15.101(c),?THIS NOTICE?DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE IN DETERMINING ITS ACQUISITION APPROACH.? THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH.? 1.3 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES Interested firms should submit information as to the capabilities, capacity, and experience to provide an MWS as set forth below: The MWS must alert the F-15EX aircrew to the presence of missiles that may threaten the aircraft without unreasonably distracting the aircrew with false alarms. The MWS must use the six (6) pre-existing F-15EX sensor locations, data cables, power cables, and cooling. It must be easily, safely, rapidly, and organically installable and removable in the field by USAF military aircraft maintenance personnel without requiring any change to aircraft configuration beyond installation of MWS line replaceable units (LRUs) in the six (6) pre-existing locations in the aircraft dedicated for missile warning. To avoid compromise of classified information, this notice does not ask for threat missile launch and approach detection performance for various use cases nor for an MWS concept of operations. AFLCMC/WAQ may contact you to ask for detection performance information if your response to this Sources Sought notice indicates your MWS is integrable in an F-15EX aircraft. Questions: What is the name of the MWS you describe in your response to this Sources Sought notice? Please include titles, abbreviations, and nomenclature as available. Please only identify and describe a single MWS in your response. On what Department of War (DoW) aircraft model(s) is your MWS approved for operational use today? Approval for operational use requires both 1) determination of airworthiness of the aircraft with your MWS integrated and 2) sustainment of the aircraft�s cybersecurity Authorization to Operate. Who are the best references (name, position, organization, commercial telephone number, and US Government email address) for DoW acquirers responsible for procuring your MWS for operational use on DoW aircraft named in question 2? Is your MWS in active production today? How many months from contract award could your MWS be delivered? Does your MWS consist only of sensor LRUs or does your MWS consist of sensor LRUs connected to a central processing LRU? If MWS sensors are connected to a central processor, how are they connected? What are the dimensions of each LRU in your MWS? You are alternately welcome to include in your response figures from engineering drawings that identify dimensions, rather than listing dimensions. How much does each LRU in your MWS weigh? How are your MWS�s LRUs physically fastened to an aircraft? What are your MWS�s electrical power requirements? Through what cable connection(s) is your MWS powered by the aircraft? What are your MWS�s cooling requirements? Through what interface(s) is your MWS cooled by the aircraft? Can your MWS be connected to an aircraft�s MIL-STD-1553 avionics bus? What are the terms by which your firm will share the MIL-STD-1553 avionics bus interface specification for your MWS with The Boeing Company so data can be exchanged between your MWS and the F-15EX�s onboard mission computer? Does your MWS require the aircrew or maintenance personnel to provide information to your MWS during aircraft preflight or midflight for it to correctly detect missiles that may threaten the aircraft? If so, how is this information provided to your MWS? Does the installation on, operation of, or removal of your MWS from an aircraft expose personnel to a known health or safety hazard? Are there any known limitations on your MWS�s use in the F-15EX aircraft�s operational environment as verified in accordance with MIL-STD-810H? Does a field-executable procedure exist today for verifying the correct operation of your MWS during aircraft preflight or periodic inspection? If so, please briefly summarize the procedure. Does installation or removal of your MWS require any specific tools that are not commercially available? If yes, please identify the tools and tool vendors. Are there any known limitations on your MWS� storage environment when MWS LRUs are not installed on an aircraft? description: The purpose of amendment no. 2 is to respond to the following questions. Question-4. Is MARAD open to all forms of propulsion to gain fuel efficiencies - for example, hybrid diesel-electric equipment with electric motors and batteries? Response-4. There are no limits or specific requirements for the type of propulsion or fuel. Technologies, including fuels and propulsion, should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Question-5. Under the Eligibility Information section of the subject notice, it states that the opportunity is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." In reviewing the statutory definition of a �domestic source� under 50 U.S.C. � 4555(7), �the term �domestic source� means a business concern� (A) that performs in the United States or Canada substantially all of the research and development, engineering, manufacturing, and production activities required of such business concern under a contract with the United States relating to a critical component or a critical technology item.� Based on this definition, which appears to include qualifying Canadian businesses as domestic sources for certain USG Response-5. For the purposes of this RFP a domestic applicant is considered to be a contractor organized or existing under the laws of the United States. Keep in mind that the RFP states preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag; the RFP does not exclude those with team leads or team members outside the U.S. " Question-6. Confidentiality of design information: Our understanding is that the final report and presentation will be publicly shared, while sensitive supporting information, such as calculations, design plans and drawings, modeling results, technology details, and cost information, can be provided to MARAD without being made public. The terms and conditions, however, grant MARAD broad rights to reproduce, distribute, and display project materials. Could you clarify whether sensitive design information submitted during the project can be designated and maintained as confidential, and whether MARAD�s rights to distribute it would be limited? Response-6. Confidential business information or sensitive design information will not be shared publicly without permission. Prior to publication, MARAD and the project team will discuss the extent and limits of the information that will be shared. Question-7. Subcontracting limits: Are there any restrictions on the value or proportion of work that may be subcontracted to organizations outside the named project team, such as model testing facilities or noise specialists? Response-7. The proposed project team should include all intended team members including those that would be subcontracted such as testing facilities or noise specialists. The specifics of subcontract awards are not determined by the MARAD project manager. Question-8. Work outside the United States: May project funds be used to subcontract specialized work outside the United States? If so, are there limits on the type or value of that work? Response-8. The proposed project team should include all proposed team members. Preference will be given to those team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag. There is no specific requirement for subcontractors. ========================================================= The purpose for this amendment is to respond to the following questions: Question-1. Domestic Applicant Definition: Section D.1 of the RFP states the Challenge is "open to all types of domestic applicants other than individuals." Our company is a U.S.-registered entity, though its ultimate parents are in Canada and Europe. Could you confirm whether an entity with this ownership structure qualifies as a "domestic applicant" for purposes of serving as the lead applicant/Recipient of a cooperative agreement under this RFP? Response-1. For the purposes of this project, a U.S. registered entity will be evaluated as a domestic applicant. Question-2. Citizenship-Based Funding Restriction: We understand that MARAD/META cooperative agreements may include a restriction on using award funds for "work to be done or done in a facility owned by someone other than a Citizen of the United States (as defined in 46 C.F.R. � 315.3(b))." Could you confirm whether this restriction, or an equivalent, will apply to cooperative agreements resulting from this RFP, and if so, how it would apply to a design team whose naval architecture/engineering firm is U.S.-registered and performs all work domestically, but has foreign parent ownership? Response-2. For the purposes of this project, a design team located in the U.S. working at a U.S.-registered firm and performing all work domestically would not fall under the restriction. Question-3. Team Lead Eligibility vs. Preference: Section B notes a preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag." Could you confirm whether this operates solely as an evaluative preference, or whether it functions as a disqualifying eligibility criterion for a team lead whose ultimate parent is a foreign entity? Response-3. The preference for "team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag" is an evaluative preference. A U.S. registered entity with U.S. offices and staff performing work domestically, would fall under consideration as a domestic applicant for this project. ======================================================================= U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration�s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations a

description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration�s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team�s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only �lead� one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating �leads� will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. Le présent appel d'offres a pour objet la conclusion d'un contrat-cadre portant sur l'achat et la livraison directe de fournitures de bureau à différents sites de l'administration cantonale. Afin d'uniformiser la gamme de fournitures de bureau et de garantir la comparabilité des offres, une gamme de référence est définie.

description: Bergen municipality, the Development Department, hereby invites tenderers to a competition for a contract for a turnkey contract in the project U2940 Storetveit School. Storetveit secondary school needs upgrading and expanded capacity to meet the current educational and technical requirements, in addition to the expected increase in pupil numbers. title: Norway – Research services – Openness and inclusion - police interaction with the entire population
description: The aim of the research assignment is to obtain knowledge about how different groups of the population experience the police, what conditions affect the interaction between police and inhabitants, and how the police can ensure that different perspectives and experiences are heard and safeguarded. There is a need for knowledge about whether there are groups that find that they are not heard, how the police reach out to groups that to a small degree contact the police on their own initiative and how different forms of communication and dialogue are experienced by different groups. The research shall provide a better knowledge basis for how the police can strengthen the dialogue with the population, adapt communication and work forms to different target groups and develop services that safeguard legal security, equal treatment and high quality. The research shall also contribute with knowledge on the connection between transparency, inclusion, trust and the police's legitimacy, as well as the impact this can have on society's resilience. See further information in the tender documentation.
